biggest_gap.title: In the shipped deployment every client still has the gateway's address. Five anonymous wrong passwords keep a password user out on any new device for 15 minutes, and 30 anonymous requests a minute stop every sign-in in every workspace
biggest_gap.detail:
Round 11's gap is only partly fixed. Two things now work, and the administrator can see what is happening:
- A valid set-up code signs in while the gateway address is paused (attacks/setup-code-paused.txt: 409 'choose a new password', then 200).
- A browser that signed in before (device cookie) still signs in (200).
- The sign-in history and the paused list label 172.22.0.1 'shared gateway' in English and 'بوابة مشتركة' in Arabic. They tell the admin to give a new set-up code (screenshots 04 and 05).

The root cause is unchanged: the one-command deployment does not see real client addresses, and the fix covers only two kinds of client. An anonymous script sends 5 wrong passwords for the finance manager's e-mail. After that, their right password from a new laptop, a fresh browser or cleared cookies answers 429 for 15 minutes (Retry-After 900). The message says 'Too many failed sign-ins ... from this device', although that device never failed (screenshot 12). The script can repeat this every 15 minutes, indefinitely.

The only way back in is for an administrator to reset the user's password to a set-up code each time. That throws away their password, and it still does not help on the next new device.

Worse, and new evidence this round: the sign-in rate limit (Erp:RateLimits:SignInPerMinute, 30, partitioned by remote address in ErpPlatform) also sees one client. 30 anonymous requests to /api/auth/sign-in at unknown addresses in 3.5 s were enough. After them, the next correct sign-ins of admin@gulfsteel.example and admin@alnoor.example from other browsers both answered 429 request.tooMany (attacks/global-rate.txt). In the shipped deployment, one script stops every user of every workspace from signing in. Without any attacker, a 40-person trading company signing in at 8 a.m. would also hit it.

UAE trading and manufacturing companies often sit behind one office NAT and log in at shift start. Odoo behind its usual proxy setup does not fall into this, so this is the one thing that most holds p03 back.

Fix:
- Ship the compose deployment with a reverse proxy that forwards the client address, with ERP_KNOWN_PROXIES set by default. Or publish the port with host networking or a proxy that preserves the source.
- Partition both the pause and the rate limit by a stronger client key when the address is shared.
- Add a test: behind one shared address, a second client with no device cookie still signs in with its right password after another client's 5 failures and 30 requests.
